title: The follow-through pipeline — one intake, due conditions, and section 0 of the brief
note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-21: 'there's too many things here that get just dropped halfway through... not just more CI guards or whatever, not just building up the CLAUDE.md -- actually creating infra that has a pipeline that pulls things through to the finish.' THIS IS THE UNSOLVED PROBLEM THE RESET HAS SO FAR ONLY RELOCATED: archiving the registers removed where work rotted and did not build what pulls it through, so until this lands follow-through is WORSE than before -- the rows are in git history and nothing reads them. Design: plan section 3b. The pull is a scheduled render into the brief's section 0 plus a required same-day disposition, NOT a guard. The forcing function is that an unrouted due item appears on the OPERATOR'S page every day until routed, and the unrouted count is a number in section 5 -- which is the one structural difference from DUE.md, whose due-list was read by machinery that was read by nobody. [!] PART ONE BUILT 2026-09-21: scripts/ops/pipeline.py (the store, the validator, is_due/due/unrouted_count, render_section_0), docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl seeded EMPTY, tests/test_pipeline.py, and pipeline-guard wired into run_guards.py the same day -- a module nothing runs is the declared-capability-with-no-consumer antipattern. Each of the five drop-reasons from plan 3b is asserted by a named self-test check with a negative control, so a later session cannot loosen one without turning a check red. [!] WHAT IS NOT DONE, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS: nothing runs render_section_0 ON A SCHEDULE, because the brief that displays it is A3 and A3 is not built. Asking is therefore still VOLUNTARY, which is reason (5) -- the exact thing that killed DUE.md ('a reminder is not a mechanism'). A7 CANNOT BE CLOSED until section 0 renders on the operator's own page and the unrouted count appears as a number in section 5. Do not mark this done on the store alone. [!] The store is seeded EMPTY deliberately. Importing the 91 OPEN-ITEMS rows and 1,065 backlog rows is A8; dumping them in untriaged would fill section 0 with rows nobody dispositioned, which is the failure this replaces rather than a fast start. [!] A3a DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 (session_01AR9SV7kwUg8YBq38UVuVSN) as the lane that can close this. THAT LANE ALONE STILL DOES NOT CLOSE IT: it builds the generator, the route and the schedule in the BOT repo, and section 0 has to reach the OPERATOR'S page, which is the Svelte SPA in ict-trader-dashboard. The dashboard half (A3b) is not yet dispatched. Do not read a merged A3a PR as A7 done. [!] SECTION 0 FIRED FOR REAL ON ITS FIRST DAY, 2026-09-21, and that is the first evidence this mechanism does anything. PI-20260921-0001 (the trainer-VM serialization risk) sat `queued` and unrouted; it appeared in render_section_0's output; it was routed to a lane THE SAME DAY; unrouted went 1 -> 0. Three further items (0002/0003/0004) were filed and routed the same way within the hour. [!] THAT IS STILL NOT A7 DONE. Every one of those pulls happened because THIS session chose to run render_section_0 -- which is reason (5) verbatim, the voluntary ask that killed DUE.md. The mechanism has been shown to WORK; it has not been shown to FIRE WITHOUT BEING ASKED. Only A3 closes that, and only when the operator's own page shows it. [!] LANE FIELD SET AT CLOSE-OUT 2026-09-21 — it was null while A3a was the live lane against this row, which reads as 'nobody is on it'. [!] STILL OPEN AFTER A3a MERGED, and this is the distinction the row exists to protect. The brief now renders §0 from pipeline.py and carries the unrouted count as a number — but only to whoever RUNS it. A7 closes when it reaches the operator's own page, which is the SPA, which is A3b, which is not dispatched. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-21 — OBSERVED, not inferred. The OPERATOR loaded the live Workflow page and section 0 was rendering there, and sent the screenshot: 'Today's brief · 2026-09-21' with §0 — WHAT CAME DUE, '93 item(s) due. Each needs a disposition today.', the real OI-* rows beneath it, and the headline band reading 85 UNROUTED · 93 DUE · 1,168 ITEM(S) · 1,182 RECORD(S) · PIPELINE: READ · CHECKLIST: READ · MANDATES: ABSENT. [!] THAT IS THE EXACT OBSERVATION THIS ROW HELD OUT FOR and the one no session could make: headless verification of the deployed Pages URL does not work from a sandbox (measured 2026-09-11). The pull is now INVOLUNTARY — an unrouted due item appears on the page the operator already opens, whether or not anyone chose to look. That is reason (5) answered, which is what killed DUE.md. [!] NOTE the read-states render DISTINGUISHABLE on the page rather than collapsed: MANDATES: ABSENT is shown amber and separately from PIPELINE: READ, so 'we could not look' and 'we looked and found nothing' stay apart end to end, from pipeline.py through the route to the render.
